strengths: Compelling motivation to address the autoencoder bottleneck in latent diffusion models (lossy reconstruction, separate two-stage optimization, and error accumulation during editing) by training diffusion transformers directly in pixel space.

Well-designed and efficient dual-level transformer architecture: decoupling semantic processing at the patch level from detail refinement at the pixel level via pixel-wise AdaLN modulation and pixel token compaction keeps computational complexity (311 GFLOPs) close to latent models.

Impressive performance across benchmarks: achieves 1.61 gFID on ImageNet 256x256, substantially improving upon prior pixel-space diffusion models, and scales to 1024x1024 text-to-image generation with competitive GenEval (0.74) and DPG-bench (83.5) scores.

Clear illustration of the intrinsic benefits of pixel-space generation, particularly showing preserved background high-frequency details (e.g., text on walls) during train-free editing where latent VAEs induce noticeable non-invertible reconstruction degradation.
Comprehensive and thorough empirical analysis, including ablations on patch sizes, layer depth allocation (N vs. M), compaction rates, guidance intervals, and ODE samplers.
weaknesses: The core PiT compaction mechanism compresses $p^2 \times D_{\text{pix}}$ into a single token of dimension $D$ for global multi-head self-attention. Because attention is computed over the patch sequence length $L$, the pixel-level pathway operates similarly to an additional patch-level transformer coupled with a learned per-pixel expansion and AdaLN. Further discussion and comparison against alternative local detail refinement modules (e.g., local window attention or lightweight convolutions) would provide deeper insight into why global compaction is the optimal choice.

The training pipeline incorporates the REPA objective (aligning intermediate representations with DINOv2 features), which is known to heavily boost convergence and FID scores in modern DiT architectures. While ablations in Table 4 examine architectural components, isolating the specific quantitative contribution of DINOv2 alignment versus the architectural pixel modeling improvements would improve attribution of gains.

In the text-to-image experiments, the model is trained on a proprietary/internal 26M image-text dataset. Providing further details regarding data filtering, aesthetic scoring, and captioning methodology would enhance reproducibility and contextualize the comparison with baselines trained on standard open datasets.

strengths: Revisiting pixel-space diffusion is of high interest to the generative modeling community, as avoiding VAEs bypasses lossy compression artifacts, texture blurring, and representation misalignment.

The proposed dual-level architecture is conceptually clean and well-motivated: separating semantic global reasoning (patch-level DiT) from dense detail synthesis (pixel-level DiT) via pixel-wise AdaLN and pixel token compaction effectively overcomes the quadratic computational bottleneck of full-resolution attention.
Empirical results are strong: achieving 1.61 gFID on ImageNet 256×256 sets a new state-of-the-art among pixel-space generative diffusion models at comparable model capacity and compute (311 GFLOPs).

Scaling directly to 1024×1024 pixel-space text-to-image generation is a notable achievement, yielding competitive GenEval (0.74) and DPG-bench (83.5) scores with practical inference throughput (0.33 samples/s).
The paper is thorough in its ablation studies, covering component contributions, depth allocations between pathways (N vs. M), patch size trade-offs, and compaction ratios.
weaknesses: The training pipeline incorporates a representation alignment loss with a frozen DINOv2 encoder (REPA). It is unclear how much of the performance advantage (e.g., convergence speed and final FID) stems from DINOv2 feature guidance versus the architectural innovations; an ablation isolating the contribution of REPA on PixelDiT would strengthen the technical attribution.

While the qualitative demonstration of image editing (Figure 1b) clearly highlights the benefit of bypassing VAE reconstruction artifacts, the evaluation is anecdotal. Quantitative metrics on standard image editing benchmarks (such as background preservation and prompt-directed edit precision) are lacking.

Details on the training computational overhead (e.g., total GPU hours / hardware budget for the 26M image T2I model pretraining and 1024x1024 finetuning) are not thoroughly reported, making it difficult to directly assess the training efficiency trade-off compared to latent diffusion pipelines.

strengths: Significant milestone in pixel-space generative modeling: The paper successfully scales a transformer-based pixel diffusion model directly up to 1024x1024 resolution for text-to-image generation, achieving strong prompt alignment and benchmark scores (0.74 GenEval, 83.5 DPG-Bench) without relying on a pre-trained VAE.

Well-motivated and effective architecture: The dual-level decoupling—handling semantic structure via coarse patch tokens and dense detail refinement via a compact pixel-level pathway (PiT with low hidden dimension D_pix=16)—is elegant. The pixel-wise AdaLN and pixel token compaction allow the model to retain per-pixel responsiveness while avoiding quadratic attention complexity over raw pixels.

Strong performance and computational efficiency: On ImageNet 256x256, PixelDiT achieves an FID of 1.61 with only 311 GFLOPs, outperforming recent pixel-space models (PixelFlow, PixNerd, JiT) and closing the performance gap to latent diffusion models while remaining highly computationally competitive.

Clear demonstration of the advantages of pixel-space modeling: The FlowEdit application (Figure 1b) clearly showcases the tangible benefit of eliminating VAEs, preserving fine background details (e.g., small scene text) that are typically distorted by lossy latent autoencoders.

Thorough ablation and empirical analysis: The manuscript includes comprehensive investigations into patch sizes, allocation of depth between patch and pixel stages (N vs. M), compaction compression ratios, sampler comparisons, and CFG intervals.
weaknesses: Evaluation of image editing is purely anecdotal: The paper highlights VAE-free detail preservation in image editing as a primary motivation, but supports this claim with only a single qualitative comparison in Figure 1b. A systematic benchmark with quantitative metrics (e.g., background PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS, CLIP text-image similarity) across diverse editing prompts would substantially substantiate this claim.

Confounding effect of representation alignment (REPA): The training formulation incorporates representation alignment loss with a frozen DINOv2 backbone. Because REPA is known to significantly boost convergence and FID in DiTs, an explicit ablation isolating the dual-level architecture with and without REPA is needed to clarify how much gain arises from the architecture versus the feature guidance.

Conceptual overlap with prior multi-rate / patch-compression architectures: In the pixel transformer (PiT) block, compressing p^2 pixels into a single token via learned flattening means self-attention in PiT operates at the exact same sequence length L as the patch pathway. A deeper conceptual comparison with hierarchical diffusion frameworks (such as DDT, Würstchen, and PixNerd) regarding the specific role of PiT attention versus standard convolutional/local refinement would provide clearer positioning.

Limited dataset details for the T2I model: The text-to-image model is trained on a proprietary/collected set of 26M image-text pairs, but details regarding filtering pipelines, source distributions, and synthetic captioning are sparse, making full experimental reproducibility challenging.

strengths: Compelling Milestone for Pixel-Space Diffusion: The paper successfully closes the performance and efficiency gap between pixel-space diffusion and latent diffusion models (LDMs), achieving a state-of-the-art FID of 1.61 on ImageNet 256x256 and 1.81 on ImageNet 512x512 among pixel generative models, while scaling directly to 1024x1024 text-to-image synthesis.

Well-Motivated and Elegant Architectural Design: The dual-level architecture effectively disentangles coarse semantic reasoning (at a large patch size p=16) from dense texture refinement. The combination of Pixel Token Compaction (compress-attend-expand) and Pixel-wise AdaLN modulation overcomes the quadratic memory/FLOPs bottleneck of naive pixel-level attention while allowing spatially distinct, high-frequency modulations.

Practical Downstream Advantages over LDMs: The manuscript convincingly demonstrates a concrete failure mode of latent diffusion models—lossy VAE compression distorting fine background details and text—and shows that PixelDiT inherently preserves unedited background fidelity in training-free image editing (achieving significantly lower MSE and higher SSIM on FlowEdit benchmarks).

Extensive and Transparent Empirical Evaluation: The paper contains thorough ablations covering depth allocation (N vs. M), patch size scalability, token compaction ratios, guidance scheduling, and inference solvers. Additionally, Section G provides exceptionally valuable negative results and design insights (e.g., DCT basis modulation, Haar transforms, cross-attention vs. AdaLN), which greatly benefits the community.
weaknesses: Heavy Reliance on Auxiliary Feature Alignment (REPA): The ablation in Table 11 and discussion in Section G.3 indicate that representation alignment with a frozen DINOv2 encoder is critical for stability and performance (without REPA, 80-epoch FID degrades from 2.36 to 6.58, and training is prone to divergence). While common in recent DiT works, this reliance means the framework depends heavily on a strong pre-trained semantic foundation rather than learning semantics purely from pixels.

Computational Scaling at 1024x1024: Although the 256x256 computational footprint is very competitive (311 GFLOPs), Table 16 indicates that at 1024x1024 resolution, forward pass complexity scales to 7,147 GFLOPs for p=16. While sampling throughput remains reasonable (0.33 samples/s), pixel-space training and inference compute at megapixel scale remains noticeably heavier than high-compression latent models.

Parameter Overhead of Pixel-wise AdaLN: The linear projection for pixel-wise AdaLN maps D to p^2 * 6 * D_pix, which scales linearly with the patch area p^2. As acknowledged in the appendix, this limits the depth of the pixel-level pathway (M=2 or 4) to avoid excessive parameter growth.

strengths: Revisiting pixel-space diffusion to eliminate the lossy autoencoder bottleneck is an important and timely direction, overcoming persistent issues in latent diffusion models such as high-frequency detail loss and reconstruction-generation distribution shift.

The proposed dual-level transformer design—combining a semantic patch-level DiT with an efficient pixel-level DiT via pixel-wise AdaLN and linear token compaction—elegantly sidesteps the quadratic token bottleneck while retaining dense local texture control.

Strong empirical results across benchmarks: achieves 1.61 FID on ImageNet 256x256 and 1.81 FID on ImageNet 512x512, outperforming prior pixel-space generative methods and rivaling established latent diffusion models, while scaling directly to 1024x1024 text-to-image synthesis.

Convincing demonstration of practical benefits in image editing, showing that bypassing VAE encoding preserves high-frequency background text and textures significantly better than SD3 and FLUX in FlowEdit evaluations.
Extensive ablation studies and honest reporting of design iterations, including negative empirical results (Appendix G), which provide valuable engineering insights for the diffusion community.
weaknesses: Critical reliance on representation alignment (REPA): As shown in Table 11 and Appendix G.3, training without the auxiliary frozen DINOv2 alignment loss causes substantial performance degradation (FID worsens from 2.36 to 6.58 at 80 epochs) and instability/divergence. This suggests the architecture does not yet learn semantic layout entirely end-to-end from scratch in pure pixel space.

Conceptual similarity to patchification: The pixel token compaction operator linearly projects a patch of pixels into a compact vector before attention and projects it back afterwards. This compress-attend-expand mechanism closely resembles patchification with residual skip connections, making the theoretical distinction from multi-scale patch transformers somewhat incremental.

Evaluation on text-to-image is limited to automated benchmarks (GenEval and DPG-Bench) trained on an internal 26M dataset. A qualitative or user-study comparison against comparably sized open-source models on fine-grained human anatomy and complex prompt composition would provide a more complete assessment of fidelity.

strengths: Compelling motivation and paradigm shift: By revisiting single-stage pixel-space diffusion, the paper directly tackles the persistent reconstruction bottleneck and artifact accumulation inherent to lossy VAEs in Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs), showing clear advantages in detail-sensitive downstream tasks such as training-free image editing.

Efficient and well-motivated architecture: The dual-level DiT design smartly disentangles high-level semantic reasoning (handled by a coarse patch-level pathway) from dense detail synthesis (handled by a lightweight pixel-level pathway). The combination of pixel-wise AdaLN modulation and pixel token compaction allows the model to process pixel-level information with manageable computational complexity (311 GFLOPs on ImageNet 256x256, on par with latent models).

Strong empirical performance across multiple benchmarks: PixelDiT achieves state-of-the-art results among pixel-space generative models on ImageNet 256x256 (1.61 gFID) and ImageNet 512x512 (1.81 gFID), outperforming previous pixel-space models (PixelFlow, PixNerd, JiT) and closing the gap to top latent models. Scaling to 1024x1024 text-to-image generation yields impressive fidelity and competitive GenEval (0.74) and DPG-Bench (83.5) scores.

Thorough ablations and transparent reporting: The experimental evaluation is comprehensive, covering architectural depth allocation, patch sizes, compaction ratios, sampling solvers, guidance intervals, and inference steps. The inclusion of negative results and failed attempts in Appendix G is commendable and provides valuable practical insights for the community.
weaknesses: Heavy reliance on pretrained representations (REPA): As demonstrated in Table 11 and Section G.3, the representation alignment loss with a frozen DINOv2 encoder is critical for stability; without it, FID degrades drastically (from 2.36 to 6.58 at 80 epochs) and training risks divergence. While the model eliminates a VAE, it still relies substantially on an external vision foundation model to guide generative learning.

Nature of pixel token compaction: Since pixel token compaction compresses $p^2$ pixels down to a single patch token before the PiT self-attention, the global attention mechanism in the pixel pathway still operates at the downsampled patch resolution $L = (H/p)(W/p)$. The per-pixel refinement relies primarily on local linear expansion and per-pixel AdaLN modulation, which resembles a lightweight decoder head rather than true long-range pixel-to-pixel interaction.

Training stability challenges: The authors note that pixel-space velocity-matching diffusion remains prone to loss spikes during extended training runs and deeper configurations, requiring sensitive gradient clipping and optimization tuning.

Evaluation breadth on editing: While the training-free editing result with FlowEdit (Figure 1b and Table 14) nicely highlights the avoidance of VAE blur/distortion, the evaluation is primarily focused on background preservation metrics (MSE/SSIM). Quantitative assessment of prompt-following/editing fidelity in the edited foreground region across standard editing benchmarks would provide a more complete picture.
